title: Brains vs Hands: How to Run AI Agents Safely in Production — Viren Baraiya
talk_summary: The talk argues production agents should be structured as harnesses: LLM brains plan, deterministic hands execute, with durable state, idempotency, and human gates. It demos an SRE loop where an agent proposes steps that are compiled into a deterministic workflow and executed iteratively.

takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM only plans the next steps; a deterministic harness validates and executes actions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the responsibility of a non-deterministic agent is to plan, is to plan what should happen next, not really to do things

takeaways.what_they_do: An agent proposes a sequence of steps, then a plan-and-compile tool turns it into a runnable deterministic workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This gets compiled into a very deterministic workflow.

takeaways.technique: Durable run state and side-effect ledger
takeaways.what_they_do: The harness tracks completed work and recorded side effects, and makes actions idempotent or records when they are not.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what has been recorded in terms of the side effects

takeaways.what_they_do: High-risk actions require a code-enforced human gate rather than LLM discretion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I probably want to have a human gate

takeaways.what_they_do: Split agents/harnesses by responsibility and give them a finite deterministic tool set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the last thing you want is to have an agent be responsible for multiple things

takeaways.what_they_do: Background, event-driven, and long-running coordinator agents monitor work and nudge stuck agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would like to have an agent monitoring that agent
